correctness.rationale: Reconstructed full argument: a finite isotone partial self-map has no periodic orbit of length>1 and is nilpotent iff fixed-point-free; a nilpotent full-domain map cannot exist. With missing m, fixed-point-free + weak isotonicity force i<f(i)<=m on the left and m<=f(i)<i on the right, with m the common boundary image. Reverse/complement and shift convert the two sides to weakly increasing parking sequences 1<=x_j<=j; their distinct-value counts are Narayana. First-return Dyck paths give u=z(1+u)(1+tu), and Lagrange inversion gives the displayed coefficients. Direct INDEPENDENT weakly increasing map enumeration for every n=2..8 matched each rank, and the Catalan totals. Boundary n=1 handled separately. This finite experiment corroborates but does not prove the all-n enumeration.

broader_coverage.reasoning: 2013 Laradji–Umar Theorem 3.8 gives J(n,r)=binom(n,r)binom(n-1,r-1)/(n-r+1) for order-decreasing FULL transformations; Theorems 3.12–3.14 address all partial isotone maps. These domains and output ranks differ, and a stronger joint restriction theorem has not been found.

value.rationale: The maximal possible nilpotent domain is an intrinsic extremal subsemigroup stratum, and image rank is a fundamental transformation invariant. This exact uniform rank distribution with a reversible missing-point/Narayana factorization is a motivated structural count, rather than an arbitrary parameter slice; a future semigroup enumerator can use the precise coefficient distribution.

final_claim: For every n>=2, the largest nilpotent domain size in PO_n is n-1; the rank-r count is N(n,r)=2/(n-1)*binom(n,r+1)*binom(n-1,r-1), r=1..n-1, with omitted-point polynomial t*C_{m-1}(t)*C_{n-m}(t) and total Catalan(n).
limitations: No claim for smaller nilpotent domains or nilpotency-index distribution.
OEIS Catalan/Narayana counts themselves are not new.
Full-text priority uncertainty for Garba 1994 and Laradji–Umar 2004.
